From Targets
to Action

Building Compass, a tool that helped Account Managers convert quarterly revenue targets into realistic execution plans using historical data and forecasting.

Quarterly revenue targets define what needs to be achieved, but they don't always explain how to achieve them.

This project turned three years of historical business data into an intelligence platform that helped Account Managers identify priority accounts, forecast expected revenue and create structured monthly plans to reach their targets with greater confidence.

Business context

Targets were clear.
The path to them wasn't.

Every quarter, Account Managers were assigned revenue targets. The targets clearly defined the expected outcome, but planning the journey towards them often depended on manually analysing historical data, individual experience and personal judgement.

Questions like these came up at the start of every quarter, and each one took real effort to answer:

Which accounts should I focus on? Which customers are most likely to grow? Which accounts can realistically contribute to my target? How much revenue should I aim for every month? Am I on track to achieve my quarterly goal?

Answering them required significant manual work and often resulted in inconsistent planning across the team.

In larger organizations, teams usually have dedicated planning tools, forecasting models and sales operations support to answer these questions. As the business continued to grow, there was an opportunity to build a single planning tool that converted existing business data into practical recommendations for Account Managers.

The objective wasn't to replace experience. It was to make planning faster, more consistent and more data-driven.

Business challenges

Four gaps that made planning harder than it needed to be

Targets without direction

Quarterly goals were assigned, but there wasn't a structured way to translate them into an execution plan.

Historical data was underutilized

Three years of account-level performance data existed but wasn't being used to support planning decisions.

No monthly planning

Quarterly targets weren't broken into realistic month-by-month milestones, making it difficult to track progress.

Prioritization was difficult

Without data-backed recommendations, deciding where to spend time depended largely on individual judgement.

The solution

Building an Compass

The solution was designed as a decision-support tool for Account Managers. Using three years of historical account data, the platform analysed past performance, growth trends and seasonality to estimate future revenue opportunities.

Rather than simply showing historical reports, it generated practical recommendations that helped Account Managers understand:

  • which accounts deserved immediate attention
  • expected revenue from individual accounts
  • monthly revenue goals
  • forecasted quarterly achievement
  • account-level growth opportunities
The objective was not to build another dashboard. It was to build a planning tool that made everyday decision-making easier.

Forecasting logic

The thinking behind the numbers

The logic was kept deliberately explainable. An Account Manager should be able to defend any number the tool produces in a review meeting.

01

Historical account performance

Every account is read on its own history rather than a portfolio average. Three financial years of revenue give a baseline of what the account normally delivers.

02

Year-over-year growth

Comparing each year against the previous one separates accounts that are genuinely expanding from accounts that had one strong year.

03

CAGR-based forecasting

A compounded growth rate smooths out single-year spikes and gives a steadier view of the pace an account has been growing at.

04

Seasonality

Most portfolios do not earn evenly across twelve months. The tool reads each account's monthly pattern so plans reflect how business actually arrives.

05

Monthly revenue distribution

The annual number is spread across months using that seasonal shape, so a slow month is planned as a slow month instead of a missed one.

06

Expected revenue

Growth rate applied to the account's base gives a natural expectation — what the account should deliver if things continue as they have.

07

Quarterly target allocation

The gap between the natural forecast and the assigned target is distributed across accounts and quarters, so the stretch sits where it is achievable.

08

Priority account identification

Accounts are grouped by strategy — push hard, grow steadily, maintain, protect — based on size, momentum and the contribution they can make to the target.

Key learnings

Information alone doesn't improve decisions

One of the biggest learnings from this project was that information alone doesn't improve decision-making. People need clarity on what actions to take.

The biggest challenge wasn't building the forecasting model. It was presenting historical business data in a way that helped Account Managers quickly understand where to focus and how to plan their quarter.

A good internal tool doesn't just display numbers. It helps people make better decisions with confidence.
